info.name: WinX88 - Mobile App API
info.description:
Player-facing API for the WinX88 mobile app.

## Setup
1. Open **Variables** and set `baseUrl`, `username`, `password`.
2. Run **01 · Auth → POST /auth/login**. The token is saved automatically into `{{token}}`; every other request uses it.

## Auth levels
- `public` - no token needed
- `player` - requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- `optional` - works without a token; returns extra per-player fields (e.g. `isFavourite`) when one is sent

## Realtime (Socket.IO, not REST)
Namespaces, each with `auth: { token: "Bearer <jwt>" }` in the handshake:
- `/notifications` - `notification:new`, `notification:unread`
- `/wallet` - `wallet:balance`
- `/games` - `round:opened`, `round:closed`

Admin-only endpoints are deliberately excluded (298 of 476 routes).

item.name: 07 · Game Rails & Catalog
item.description:
Browsing games in the app. **All public** — a visitor must be able to look
at the lobby before registering, so none of these 401.

The `Authorization` header is present but **disabled** on each request.
Enable it and `isFavourite` becomes real for that player; leave it off and
every game is simply `false`.

## The one rule

Every game carries `kind`, `providerRef` and `gameCode`, already derived by
the server. Pass those straight to favourites and to launch. **Do not
rebuild that triple in the app** — favourites and continue-playing key on
it, and a locally-guessed one will not match, so a game favourited here
silently fails to appear in Favourites.

Launching stays per-provider: Nexus games (`kind: "NEXUS"`) launch through
`GET /nexus/launch?uuid=…`.

request.description:
Every admin-built row **with its games already resolved** — one request for the whole home screen, however many rails exist.

Rails whose filter matches nothing are omitted server-side, so you never render an empty heading.

Show a "View All" affordance when `showViewAll && totalGames > games.length`, linking to the paged endpoint below.

Titles come in both languages (`titleEn` / `titleBn`); pick by the app locale and fall back to EN.

request.description: Providers that actually have playable games of that category — for a filter row. A provider with nothing synced never appears, so a filter chip cannot open empty.

Nexus vendors with live game counts, for a vendor picker.

Counts come from the local catalogue, not from Nexus, so an unsynced vendor is absent rather than present-and-empty. `SPORTSBOOK` never appears here: it has no game list and launches through its own route.
Nexus games for one vendor. `providerCode` works as an alias for `provider`. Also accepts `type` and `search`.

request.description:
The category chips on the home screen, admin-managed.

`source` decides where each chip's games come from, and they genuinely differ — handle all five:
- `ALL` — no filter
- `SLOT_PROVIDER` — the Palace slot provider picker
- `OROPLAY_GROUP` — a key of `/oroplay/vendors/grouped`
- `CATALOG` — a `casino_games.type`, i.e. `/catalog/games?type=<value>`
- `LINK` — navigate to `value`, no picker

`iconUrl` is usually null: keep a built-in icon per `key` and treat the URL as an override.
